description: An investment committee chair must decide whether to commit corporate capital to a renewable-infrastructure private credit fund and finalize the commitment size, initial draw limit, investor restrictions, and reporting obligations, with input from risk, fund operations, and compliance.

shared_context.S1: The committee is reviewing a proposed investment in the GreenBridge Renewable Infrastructure Credit Fund.
shared_context.S2: The fund invests in senior secured loans to operating renewable-energy projects and has reported positive performance for the past three years.
shared_context.S3: The proposed investment window closes on June 30, 2026.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding investment decision.
shared_context.S5: As part of the committee's normal pre-commitment process, Maya asks portfolio risk, fund operations, and compliance to report any relevant conditions before the vote.

PF1.text: Jonas recalculated the firm's existing exposure to infrastructure credit this morning and found that portfolio policy permits no more than a $6,500,000 additional commitment to GreenBridge; he received the updated exposure file today, but it has not yet been added to the committee packet.

PF2.text: Elena confirmed with GreenBridge's administrator this week that the first capital draw on this commitment may not exceed $1,500,000 and requires 10 business days' advance notice; the administrator's confirmation is still in her operations inbox.

PF3.text: Victor found in the fund's latest limited-partner side-letter package this week that the investor must require exclusions for thermal coal and Arctic drilling and receive a look-through portfolio report within 45 days after each quarter; the side letter has not yet been logged in the compliance register.

acceptance_conditions: The GreenBridge investment must be approved.
The first capital draw must be capped at exactly $1,500,000.
The first draw must require exactly 10 business days' advance notice.
Thermal coal and Arctic drilling must be excluded from the permitted investment sectors.
A look-through portfolio report must be required within exactly 45 days after each quarter.

decisive_facts.why: The public proposal gives no portfolio-specific amount, while PF1 changes commitment_amount_usd from an unconstrained proposed amount to exactly 6500000 and supplies the risk basis that must be cited.
The public proposal has no draw mechanics, while PF2 changes first_draw_limit_usd to exactly 1500000, first_draw_notice_days to exactly 10, and requires the first_draw_control commitment.

The public proposal has no investor-specific restrictions or reporting deadline, while PF3 changes the settlement to require exactly the thermal_coal and arctic_drilling exclusions, a 45-day look-through report, and the side_letter_compliance commitment.
